You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

name: arc-slide-objects-right
description: Use when an ARC grid has colored shapes and 8 markers that appear to pack toward the right edge. Preserve shapes and slide each object right until blocked.
---

# ARC: slide objects right

Use this rule when the grid contains small colored polyominoes (often colors 2–6) and one or more single-cell 8 markers, and the demonstrated output packs them toward the right side.

## Procedure
1. Treat each connected nonzero shape as a rigid object; each isolated 8 is its own single-cell object. Do not rotate, recolor, or alter the grid dimensions.
2. Move objects horizontally right, preserving each object's rows and internal shape. An object can advance only while all its cells remain in bounds and do not overlap another object.
3. Continue until the objects are packed in a stable configuration: each object is at the rightmost position available given the other shapes and any edge/obstacles. Objects sharing rows constrain each other's final horizontal positions; objects with disjoint rows can pass/occupy overlapping columns.
4. Reconstruct the original-size grid with zeros in all vacated cells.

## Checks
- Validate that every nonzero cell belongs to exactly one original object and the output preserves every object's shape, color, and row coordinates.
- Check that no objects overlap and no object can be shifted another cell right without collision or leaving the grid.
- When multiple objects constrain each other, resolve their rightward packing from the rightmost blockers toward the left; verify against any available demonstration pair before committing to this task family.",
